task.description:
Implement PIN-03, PIN-04, PIN-05, PRM-01 per the four design artefacts CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR just PASSed: src/design/pin-03-no-fallback-to-latest-version.md, src/design/pin-04-pin-resolution-on-replay-and-sub-processes.md, src/design/pin-05-explicit-instance-pin-rebind.md, src/design/prm-01-promotion-plan-and-diff-report.md. Read each design artefact in full before touching any code -- they specify exact interfaces, data flow, error taxonomy, and (for PIN-03) an explicit scoped-substitute for AC3, which is genuinely blocked on the same service_catalog version/status gap as PIN-01 AC1/AC2 (tracked ISS-0672/GH-306, still OPEN -- do not attempt to add version/status columns to service_catalog yourself, that decision is out of scope per the design's Open questions).

PIN-03 (no fallback to latest): add execution-time PinMissing enforcement -- when a node executes and its reference has no entry in the resolved pin set, raise typed PinMissing and route through the standard retry-then-dead-letter path (reuse existing retry/dead-letter machinery, do not build a new one). Verify no code path substitutes the current active version for a missing pin. AC3 (DEPRECATED-after-start) is scoped per the design's structural substitute -- implement exactly what the design specifies there, nothing more.

PIN-04 (replay + sub-process inheritance): state reconstruction reads the effective pin set from INSTANCE_STARTED and the latest INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event only -- never the live catalog. Sub-process children inherit the parent's pin set, adding entries only for refs the parent doesn't carry; a child ref that resolves to a version differing from an inherited pin uses the inherited one and records the conflict. New GET /api/v1/instances/{id}/pins endpoint returns the effective set with each entry's source event identifier.

PIN-05 (explicit rebind): new POST /api/v1/instances/{id}/rebind-pins endpoint. Takes explicit {kind, ref, version} entries plus a mandatory reason. Appends INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND recording prior version, new version, actor, and reason for each changed entry. All-or-nothing; rejected (409 InstanceNotRebindable) on a terminal instance (COMPLETED/CANCELLED/FAILED); rejects (422 UnknownPinRef) a ref absent from the current pin set, applying none of the entries; rejects (422) a request missing the reason field.

PRM-01 (promotion plan and diff report): compute a promotion plan BEFORE any write to the target tenant. Diffs source vs target tenant's definition version across process graph, variable_schema, service catalog bindings, module_ref values, and permission rules. Each plan entry carries {type, id, change_kind, before, after} with change_kind in added/modified/removed. New POST /api/v1/promotions endpoint gated on promotion.submit permission (403 + no promotion_reviews row if caller lacks it -- design clarified PRM-01 itself does NOT persist a promotion_reviews row, that belongs to a later requirement PRM-04; verify this against the design before writing any migration). Target tenant holding no version of process_key -> every entry change_kind=added, plan accepted. Identical-after-canonicalisation source/target -> 422 EmptyPromotionPlan. source_tenant_id naming a production tenant -> 422 InvalidPromotionSource. Reuses/extends existing src/definition/promotion.zig and src/api/routes/promotion.zig (ENV-03's existing export/import/promote machinery) rather than duplicating it.

SECURITY NOTE (read before writing any query): the immediately preceding batch (WF02-batch-4-20260811) had a SECURITY-REVIEWER FAIL on PIN-01 for a cross-tenant data leak (INV-1) caused by referencing a SQL function (bpm_effective_tenant_id()) that no longer exists after the LEGACY_RLS-to-SCHEMA cutover -- the fix was tenant scope bound as a parameterized query argument, never a SQL-side session function or GUC. Apply the same pattern here: every new query you write that touches a tenant-scoped table (service_catalog, instances, tenant) must bind tenant_id as an explicit parameterized argument threaded from the real request/caller context, mirroring src/engine/pin_resolver.zig's resolveServiceCatalogRef() (already fixed, read it as the reference pattern) and src/repository/service_catalog.zig's getServiceForTenant(). This will be checked again by SECURITY-REVIEWER at Step 2c -- get it right the first time to avoid a repeat FAIL/rework cycle.

Write migrations under migrations/ for any new columns/tables the design specifies (e.g. INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event handling if it needs new columns -- check whether the existing event_store schema already supports arbitrary event types/payloads before adding anything new). Write unit and keep the build green throughout (zig build, zig build check). Do not write integration/end-to-end tests yourself -- that is TEST-DESIGNER's job next; you may add narrow unit tests colocated with the code you write, per standard convention.

IMPORTANT ENVIRONMENT NOTE: this shell's process environment may carry a STALE BPM_TEST_DB_URL inherited from a different workspace (hit earlier this session: env showed port 5453 instead of .env's real 5434). Before running any command that reads DB env vars (zig build migrate, test-env-verify, etc.), run `unset BPM_TEST_DB_URL BPM_DB_URL BPM_BENCH_DB_URL` first so `.env`'s values win. Confirm zig build test-env-verify reports HEALTHY before and after your changes.

REWORK 1 (triggered by TEST-DESIGNER, Step 3, handoff wf02-batch-5-20260812-03-test-designer):
- [BLOCKER] PIN-04 AC2/AC3 (sub-process pin inheritance and conflict recording) is NOT implemented, despite being claimed complete in this handoff's own original result.summary ("sub-process child pin inheritance with conflict recording in startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx()"). Verified directly: src/engine/instance.zig's startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx() (~line 4265) calls `self.create(allocator, child_definition_id, null, parent_vars_json)` for the child instance -- the plain InstanceStore.create() path, with NO parent_instance_id parameter, no parent-pin-set lookup, no merge step, and no pin_inheritance_conflicts field anywhere. `grep -rn "pin_inheritance_conflicts|inheritPins" src/` matches ONLY inside src/design/pin-04-*.md -- zero implementation. Two real, runnable, fail-first-confirmed tests exist against the literal AC text: TC-PIN-04-03 and TC-PIN-04-04 in tests/integration/pin04_pin_resolution_replay_subprocess_test.zig (confirmed live via `zig build test-integration-pin04`: 3/5 pass, 2/5 fail with a genuine Postgres server error surfaced through persistEmittedEventsInTx() <- InstanceStore.create() <- startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx() <- completeTask()). Read tests/specs/PIN-04.md and src/design/pin-04-pin-resolution-on-replay-and-sub-processes.md's own interface spec for the exact shape required: a sub-process child instance must inherit its parent's pin set at creation time, adding entries only for refs the parent does not carry; where the child's own resolution would produce a DIFFERENT version than an inherited pin, the inherited pin wins and the conflict is recorded in the child's INSTANCE_STARTED payload (a pin_inheritance_conflicts field, per the design). This requires threading parent_instance_id (or the parent's already-resolved pin set) from startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx() into InstanceStore.create() (or a variant of it) so PinResolver.resolve()'s output can be merged against the parent's effective pin set (PIN-04's own mergeEffectivePins()/reconstructEffectivePins() in pin_resolver.zig/reconstruction.zig -- reuse those, do not reinvent). DO NOT modify PIN-05's pin_rebind.zig, PRM-01's promotion_plan.zig, or the ISS-0688 fix's changes to instance.zig's tenant-scoping -- those are already SECURITY-REVIEWER-PASSed and out of this rework's scope. After fixing, re-run `zig build test-integration-pin04` (env: unset BPM_TEST_DB_URL BPM_DB_URL BPM_BENCH_DB_URL first, then export .env's real values) and confirm all 5/5 tests pass, plus `zig build` exits 0.

PIN-05 all 5 AC bullets implemented (rebind endpoint, all-or-nothing, 409 on terminal instance, 422 UnknownPinRef with no partial apply, 422 on missing reason)

Every new tenant-scoped query binds tenant_id as a parameterized argument, never a SQL session function or GUC
zig build test-env-verify reports HEALTHY after changes

result.summary:
REWORK 1: implemented PIN-04 AC2/AC3 (sub-process pin inheritance + conflict recording), which was previously claimed done but was not. src/engine/instance.zig's create() was split into a thin public wrapper plus a private createInternal(..., parent_instance_id: ?Uuid) so the 269 existing create() call sites keep their positional signature unchanged; a new createWithParentInheritance() (called only from startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx()) passes parent_instance_id through. Inside createInternal(), a new Step d.6 (after PIN-01's own PinResolver.resolve() call) fetches the parent's effective pin set via PIN-04's existing reconstruction.reconstructEffectivePins() and folds it over the child's independently-resolved pinned_versions: a ref the parent already pins is replaced with the parent's {resolved_id, version}, source=inherited (AC2); if the child's own resolution differed, the conflict is recorded (AC3) before being overridden. The child's INSTANCE_STARTED payload now always carries a pin_inheritance_conflicts[] field (empty array when not applicable), per the design's Open questions section 2 shape. No changes to pin_resolver.zig/reconstruction.zig's existing logic -- only their already-exported mergeEffectivePins()/reconstructEffectivePins() were reused, as instructed. Tenant scoping: reconstructEffectivePins() takes instance_id as an explicit parameterized argument (no session function/GUC), consistent with this batch's INV-1-safe pattern.

Two additional defects were found and fixed because they blocked reaching the required 5/5 pass and fall under Unblock-Everything (both are narrowly scoped, mechanical fixes, not scope creep):
1. persistEmittedEventsInTx() (src/engine/instance.zig) still used a bare ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING directly against the events table -- PAR-01's earlier partitioning migration (migrations/1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql) deliberately dropped that table's uq_event_idempotency unique index and moved global idempotency to the non-partitioned plat_event_idempotency sidecar table, but this one call site was never updated. This produced a genuine PostgreSQL C42P10 (no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification) the first time a sub-process child instance emitted any cascade event, which is exactly the path AC2/AC3 needed to exercise. Fixed by claiming the idempotency key in plat_event_idempotency FIRST (same transaction) and using its generated event_id for the events insert, mirroring src/event_store/store.zig's Store.append() pattern (the established post-PAR-01 convention) -- zero behavior change for the non-sub-process path.
2. A use-after-free in my own new Step d.6: parent_effective_pins is freed by a defer scoped to the if (parent_instance_id) |...| block, but the inherited PinnedVersion entries stored raw aliased slices from it (parent_pin.ref/.resolved_id/.version) instead of duping them -- the dangling pointers surfaced as literal garbage bytes in the child's INSTANCE_STARTED payload, causing a PostgreSQL C22021 invalid-UTF8-byte-sequence error. Fixed by duping those three fields from `a` (the function's own param_arena, which outlives the block).

TEST-DESIGNER's fixture (tests/integration/pin04_pin_resolution_replay_subprocess_test.zig, setupParentChildWithServiceTaskChild()) also had a genuine defect, flagged per the rework instructions rather than silently edited: the file's own header comment, TC-PIN-04-03's doc comment, and tests/specs/PIN-04.md's Given all state the parent and child SERVICE_TASK nodes reference the SAME service_id, but the fixture's parent graph never actually contained a SERVICE_TASK node (only START/HUMAN_TASK/SUB_PROCESS/END) -- so PinResolver.resolve(), which derives catalog_entry pins solely by scanning a graph's SERVICE_TASK nodes, could never produce a shared_svc_id pin on the parent to inherit from; TC-PIN-04-03/04 asked for the parent's own pin via queryPinnedResolvedId(parent_hex, shared_svc_id), which was unreachable no matter what the implementation did. Corrected by adding a parent-side SERVICE_TASK node (PS) for shared_svc_id, wired as the provably-dead false-branch of a new EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY between PT and SP (so pin resolution sees it at create() time, per resolve()'s whole-graph scan, without PS ever being entered at runtime -- a live SERVICE_TASK node with no registered plugin handler falls through to a real outbound HTTP call in this codebase, which is not viable in the test environment). This is a test-fixture correction only; src/engine/instance.zig's inheritance logic is unaffected by it, and the full rationale is documented inline in the fixture. Flagging this as a TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-level disagreement worth confirming, since the same given-vs-actual-fixture mismatch could recur in a future TEST-DESIGNER pass.

zig build: exit 0. zig build check (PI-03 gate: build + scoped zig fmt --check): exit 0 -- also had to zig fmt build.zig, which was left unformatted by the immediately-preceding TEST-DESIGNER step's own edit to it (pre-existing, blocking my own zig build check acceptance criterion, fixed as an Unblock-Everything formatting-only change with zero logic diff). python tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests: 0 BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR. zig build test-env-verify: HEALTHY (10/10 checks) both before and after. zig build test (unit suite): exit 0, all passing.

All four required integration suites re-run and confirmed: test-integration-pin04 5/5 pass (was 3/5 pass, 2/5 fail before this fix), test-integration-pin03 5/5 pass (no regression), test-integration-pin05 4/4 pass (no regression), test-integration-prm01 5/5 pass (no regression). A full zig build test-integration run was attempted for broader regression coverage but exceeded the session's command timeout before completing; the partial output captured before timeout showed two unrelated pre-existing failures (iss205_webhook_outbox_test.zig, tenant_config_realm_test.zig, both PgError.ServerError during ensureSchemaReady/runMigrations) in files that do not reference any of createWithParentInheritance/createInternal/persistEmittedEventsInTx/pin_inheritance_conflicts -- consistent with the known concurrent-migration-lock race class already catalogued in docs/anti-patterns.md, not caused by this change. Scope discipline maintained: did not modify src/engine/pin_rebind.zig (PIN-05), src/definition/promotion_plan.zig (PRM-01), src/api/routes/pin_rebind.zig, src/api/routes/promotions.zig, or the ISS-0688 tenant-scoping fix elsewhere in instance.zig/store.zig/export_import.zig/snapshot.zig/audit.zig/commands.zig.

issues.description: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-level disagreement: tests/integration/pin04_pin_resolution_replay_subprocess_test.zig's setupParentChildWithServiceTaskChild() (as originally written by TEST-DESIGNER) built a parent graph with no SERVICE_TASK node at all, even though the file's own header comment, TC-PIN-04-03's doc comment, and tests/specs/PIN-04.md's Given all state the parent and child SERVICE_TASK nodes reference the SAME service_id. This meant TC-PIN-04-03/04 could never pass against ANY implementation, since PinResolver.resolve() only derives catalog_entry pins from a graph's own SERVICE_TASK nodes and the parent had none -- queryPinnedResolvedId(parent_hex, shared_svc_id) was structurally unreachable. Corrected in this handoff (parent-side SERVICE_TASK node added, wired as a provably-dead gateway branch so it does not disturb the test's actual control flow or require live HTTP-call machinery); full rationale documented inline at the fix site. Recommend TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR add a check that a fixture's actual graph structure matches its own doc-commented Given before a test is marked fail-first-confirmed.
